IS : 8244 - 1976

Indian Standard
METHODS OF CALIBRATION OF VACUUM GAUGES BY DIRECT COMPARISON WITH REFERENCE GAUGE
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 October 1976, after the draft finalized by the Chemical Engineering Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 The vacuum gauges which may be calibrated by this method are of very different types: ionization vacuum gauges, either radioactive ( for example, alphatron ) or with a cold cathode or with a hot cathode ( for example, classical inverted triode, high-pressure vacuum gauge, simple Bayard-Alpert gauge, modulated Bayard-Alpert gauge, extraction gauge, hot-cathode magnetron gauge ), thermal vacuum gauges, mechanical vacuum gauges (for example, diaphragm gauge ) or partial pressure gauges. 0.3 This standard is based on Draft ISO/DIS 3567 `Vacuum gaugesCalibration by direct comparison with a reference gauge' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). 0.4 In reporting the result of a test made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies a method for calibrating direct comparison with a reference vacuum gauge. 1.1.1 The method is not limited to a particular 2. REFERENCE 2.1 The reference absolute calibrating GAUGE vacuum gauge shall be a gauge calibrated bench or an absolute gauge. . - J`! 3 . on an a vacuum gauge by pressure range.

ISr8244- 1976 3. PRINCIPLE 3.1 Two distinct cases should he considered for applying this standard: Calibration a> of a complete tiressure gauge assembly, including the gauge head and its supply and measuring units. b) Calibration of a gauge head alone under its specified condition. In this case all necessary circuits and apparatus to ensure the gauge head operation under its specified conditions and to measure the various quantities with the required accuracy shall be available.

3.2 The gauges to be calibrated and the. reference gauges are connected to a test chamber in which the required pressures are produced, as given in Appendix A. 3.3 A uniform and stable distribution of. gas in the measuring volume is achieved at the pressure tappings on this volume, so that the pressures are close enough to enable comparisons to be made with the required accuracy. 3.4 To achieve accuracy in calibration, observed. the conditions given in 4 shall be

3.4.1 The accuracy ok the calibration depends on the accuracy of the reference gauge and on the type of gauge to be calibrated. Generally, an overall accuracy of about 10 percent can be obtained. 4. APPARATUS 4.1 Reference Gauges-one or more, for use in the range of pressures within which the vacuum gauge is to be calibrated. 4.2 Vacuum System shall meet the following requirements.

4.2.1 The test chamber shall have a volume at least 20 times the total volume of the gauges and any associated plumbing connected to it. 4.2.2 The test chamber shall have a shape such that the ratio of wall surface to volume is the minimum practical (in glass apparatus, for example, a sphere ) but not greater'than that of a right cylinder having a length equal to four times its diameter. 4.2.3 Communication between the test chamber and the rest of the vacuum system shall be effected in such a way that the incoming stream does not impinge on any of the test or referepce gauges or openings .Ir, ! thereto.

ISr8244-1976
4.2.4 The reference gauges and gauges to be calibrated shall be connected to the test chamber in an arrangement in which pressure and temperature differentials do not introduce appreciable errors. The geometry of the tubing connecting the measuring chamber with the gauges shall be such that a molecule of gas emanating from the measuring chamber cannot penetrate the active zone of a gauge without having encountered a wall at least once.

4.215 The various gauges may show phenomena of sorption or desorption. In order to minimize the unbalanced pressure distribution resulting from these effects, the conductance of the tubing connecting the measuring chamber and the `gauges shall be about 100 times the volume rate of flow corresponding to the combined effect of these sorptions and desorptions which usually results in a conductance of at least several litres per second. .4.2.6 The base pressure ( that is, when no gas is introduced ) shall not exceed 2 percent of the lower limit of.the calibration range as indicated either by the reference gauge or by the gauge to be calibrated. Care shall be taken to ensure that the simultaneous functioning of the reference gauge and the gauge to be calibrated does not result in any discernible mutual influence on their respective readings in steady operation. If simultaneous calibrations are envisaged,' it shall be necessary to check by means of cross-controls that, in steady operation, there is no appreciable interaction. If such interaction exists, additional precautions shall be taken. 4.3 Ionization Gauge - actir.g as a monitor for the chamber pressure. 4.4 Buffer Volume and Monitor Garage - The monitor gauge is for This pressure indication in this buffer volume (see Appendix A). material is optional. 4.5 Calibration Gas 4.5.1 The quality of the gas shall correspond to a maximum content of impurities of 0.1 percent by volume. 4.5.2 The device for introducing the gas into the apparatus from the supply container shall be constructed and used in such a way that the purity Where practicable, the purity of the gas rate is maintained in practice. in `the system shall be monitored by a partial pressure gauge. 4.6 Thermometers 4~3.1 The-ambient temperature around the measuring chamber and the gauges shall be determined by means of thermometers suitably*posltioned and protected from radiation, with an accuracy better than 1�C. 4.6.2 The temperature of the measuring chan&er shall be measured by means of thermometers in thermal contact with it, with an accuracy better than 1�C. . -4.. I 5

IS:ti44-1976 4.6.3 Roth the reference gauges and the gauges to be calibrated shall be placed in still air and, if necessary, protected in such a way that their temperature in stationary conditions, conditioned by their operation and by the ambient temperature, remains constant within the limits spec$ied by their respective manufacturers:
5. PROCEDURE 5.1 In operating the gauges the manufacturer's instructions shall be followed, unless otherwise specified by the customer. The reference gauge shall always be used under its specified conditions. In addition, all operations shall be carried out according to accepted practice. 5.2 When the assembly is ready According to the ultimate pressure to bake out. The bake-out procedure, or the customer and the calibration for operation, pumping is started. required, it shall often be necessary as agreed between the manufacturer laboratory; shall be carried out.

5.3 If necessary, `the gauge heads shall be degassed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations or as agreed to between the customer and the calibration laboratory. 5.4 Gauges which are to be used simultaneously shall be kept in operation. Adequate time shall be allowed for the temperature of the measuring chamber to stabilize with respect to the ambient temperature. At this point the temperature of the measuring chamber and the ambient temperat.ure are noted; they shall lie between 20 and 26X, preferably at 23�C. 5.5 The measuring gas is introduced through the gas inlet adjustment valves with, the -pump valve either partially open or completely closed. In the first case, the gas flow is controlled to give a constant pressure reading of the reference gauge equal to the minimum calibration pressure. In the second case, an amount of gas is introduced such that the minimum calibration pressure is obtained in the test chamber. 5.6 After adjusting the variable and adjustable parameters of the gauge to the required values, the measuring instruments shall be stabilized so as to obtain readings constant within about 1 percent of the full-scale `electrical range of the gauge being calibrated, for an adequate period ( about 5 minutes ). 5.7 The measurements shall be carried out according to the relevant standards on the gauges to be calibrated and on the `reference gauge. These measurements, are repeated- at least twice. 5.8 The pressure in the system shall be increased so as to have a sequence of at least three calibration points for each range of the instrument or three calibration points for each power of t_eT;if the range covers more than one decade. 6 . -4.. .

IS I 8244 - 1976 These points should correspond to: regularly spaced values of the pressure for the same adjustment of the variable parameters of the gauges. 6. PRESENTATION OF RESULTS shall be stated: 6.1 The following particulars Identification of a> reference gauge,

the gauges or gauge heads, including the by the manufacturer's name, type of gauge, series and serial number for the type concerned; b) The date of calibration; cl The method of calibration and operational procedures as presented in this standard, with deviations, if any; 4 The methods used for checking the requirements of 4.2.6; 4 The accuracy of the reference gauge; f) An estimate of the overall inaccuracy of the gauge calibration; d The nature of the gas employed; and h) The temperature of the measuring chamber and the ambient temperature. 6.2 The following characteristics shall be stated: 6.2.1 Gauge Assembly --A table of the pressures ( or values of corresponding physical quantities ) read on the vacuum gauge as a function of the pressures indicated by the reference gauge, shall be drawn for each set of variable and adjustable parameter values. The table shall contain all the relevant readings, of readings for each pressure setting. that is, three sets

6.2.2 Gauge Htadr - A table of the pressures ( or values of corresponding physical quantities ) read on the vacuum gauge to be calibrated as a function of the pressures indicated by the reference gauge, for each set of variable parameter values. The table shall contain all the relevant readings, that is, .three sets of readings for each pressure setting.

The transfer gauge shall be calibrated against the reference gauge with nitrogen gas, according to the procedure given in 5. The valve to the cold .trap and the reference gauge shall be closed. The condensable vapour shall be admitted to the calibration chamber as required to establish the pressure desired for a test point. The gauges shall be calibrated over the desired range of pressures following the procedures detailed `in 5 using, however, the transfer gauge in place of the reference gauge.
